The implementation loop looked after its pull request only while its run
was open. The run parks at `await-pr`, which the `pr-ready-check` sweep
polls every two minutes, and the moment the pull request is green with
no open thread the run ends so the backlog slot frees. From then on
nothing of the loop watched the pull request: when main moved the branch
fell behind or conflicted, when main's CI changed the branch went red,
and the ticket's pull request sat there. The auto-merge loop (#3320) had
grown a fixer to cover this, `auto-merge-fix`, which merged the base in
and edited any author's branch. That is not its job: auto merge waits
and approves, and the loop that opened a pull request keeps it
mergeable.

"pull-3320" (2026-10-23T14:47:00Z) — 4 section(s):

[1] "pull-3320" section 1:
Pull request #3320 in re-cinq/lore: Auto merge loop: approve and merge every reviewed, green pull request, fixing it when it is not
State: merged
Author: gedaiu
Opened: 2026-10-23T13:45:54Z
Closed: 2026-10-23T14:47:00Z
Merged: 2026-10-23T14:47:00Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/lore/pull/3320

[2] "pull-3320" section 2:
The Auto merge loop now does the work itself instead of only listing Lore's own pull requests. With the loop switched on, every open pull request that code review has passed, whoever opened it, gets one `auto-merge` run on the external floor. The run waits until CI is green, no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and the pull request has been open for the minimum age. Red CI, a conflict or open review goes to a new `auto-merge-fix` agent, which pushes commits without rewriting history and answers each thread; its replies are posted in the threads and the settled ones resolved, three rounds at most. Then the `approve` station approves it, as the lore-reviewer App when it is installed (#3307) and as Lore's own App otherwise. On a branch whose rule asks for an approval it arms GitHub's auto-merge first and GitHub merges; on a branch with no such rule the loop merges itself, unless the pull request touches a CODEOWNERS path. Lore's own pull requests park when there is no lore-reviewer, because GitHub refuses an approval from their author.

[3] "pull-3320" section 3:
The loop's only setting is `auto_merge.min_age_hours` (24 by default), an hours field beside the switch. The approver setting, the two-key approval PR for it and the prerequisite gate are gone; the two-key ceremony still guards an agent definition's `image`. Post-review no longer arms anything. A stations sweep (`cron.auto_merge.tick`, every 5 minutes) starts at most 3 runs per repository per tick, skipping drafts, forks and pull requests a run is already working. The board reads any author: Backlog is reviewed with no run yet, Current is a run working it, Awaiting merge is armed or only waiting out its age ("merges after …"), Parked is a failed run or a person-blocked reason, and Recently addressed is what the loop merged this week. Blocked reasons now cover every pull request in a repository whose loop is on.

The spec `specs/protected-branch-merge` is rewritten for this, ADR-051 has an amendment for the one place Lore now merges, and the two-key, port, external-floor and implementation-loop specs plus CLAUDE.md follow. lore-reviewer's approval is still audited as `lore_reviewer_approved`, so the SC-001 KPI view keeps counting.

[4] "pull-3320" section 4:
Before lore-reviewer approves anything, someone has to create the App, set `enable_lore_reviewer = true` and apply terraform from main, add its three secret versions, force-sync the ExternalSecret and restart lore-stations (`docs/managing-secrets.md`). Until then the loop approves people's pull requests as Lore's App and parks Lore's own.
